description: Pedestrian Mobility Plan Pedestrian Demand is a dataset listed in City of New York open data portal (data.cityofnewyork.us), an open data portal (Socrata) of a city, published or maintained by City of New York. Based on citywide data sources for pedestrian generators, NYC DOT developed a data-driven framework to categorize streets based on pedestrian needs. The plan aims to improve pedestrian comfort and convenience as well as increase walking citywide. NYC DOT created five broad street categories to determine the pedestrian needs on the city’s sidewalks. Coverage: New York City. The portal files it under the category Transportation. Its tags are community, corridor, global, mobility, neighborhood. The table has 20 columns. Attribution on the portal: Department of Transportation (DOT). The portal shows 2026-09-22 as the last data update. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the portal listing (dataset page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support cycling and walking network and demand studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-soc-data-cityofnewyork-us-portal.
